claims.claim: DeepGEMM is an open-source DeepSeek tensor-core kernel library with FP8 GEMMs, fine-grained scaling, grouped GEMM interfaces, and pinned SM90 and SM100 implementations.

evidence.observation: The pinned project README identifies the library and its runtime-compiled tensor-core kernels, requires an SM90 or SM100 GPU, and documents dense and grouped FP8 interfaces.

challenge.alternative: DeepGEMM is one standalone Hopper teaching kernel rather than a two-architecture library.
challenge.check: Inspect the pinned repository requirements, exported interfaces, and architecture dispatch.
challenge.outcome: The repository exposes multiple kernel families and dispatches separate SM90 and SM100 implementations.

claims.claim: DeepGEMM's core kernel is about 300 lines and achieves about 90% utilization on H800.

evidence.observation: The two pinned FP8 kernel templates alone are 346 and 567 lines, while the pinned README reports only an up-to 1550 TFLOPS result and supplies no 90% utilization statement.

claims.claim: DeepSeek-V3's fine-grained FP8 scheme scales activations per 1x128 tile and weights per 128x128 block to better accommodate outliers than coarser scaling.

evidence.observation: The authors specify per-token 1x128 activation tiles and 128x128 weight blocks and say the smaller groups better accommodate outliers.

challenge.alternative: Both operands use one tensor-wide scale or the same 128x128 grouping.
challenge.check: Compare the activation and weight granularity stated in section 3.3.2 and Appendix B.2.
challenge.outcome: The paper deliberately uses asymmetric 1x128 activation and 128x128 weight groupings and reports instability for block-wise activation gradients.

claims.claim: The 1x128/128x128 scheme prevents outliers from destroying precision and always stores one FP32 scale per tile or block across both architectures.

evidence.observation: The paper makes the scoped claim that smaller groups better accommodate outliers, not an absolute guarantee that precision cannot be destroyed.
The pinned library requires FP32 scaling factors on SM90 but packed UE8M0 scaling factors on SM100, contradicting the diagram's universal FP32 labels.

claims.claim: Hopper's FP8 accumulator is approximately FP22 and DeepGEMM promotes it every Nc=128 columns, equivalent to four consecutive WGMMA operations.

evidence.observation: The authors report about 14 retained bits and define Nc=128 as 128 inner-dimension elements, equivalent to four WGMMAs; they do not characterize the accumulator as FP22 or as an output-column interval.

claims.claim: The displayed SM90 CUDA fragment is a faithful or reproducible representation of DeepGEMM's Nc=128 promotion implementation.

evidence.locator: math warp-group accumulation and Promote with scales loop
evidence.observation: The real kernel uses float accum and final_accum register arrays, issues BLOCK_K/WGMMA::K operations for one K block, waits, and applies A/B scales into final_accum. The page instead invents undefined helpers and a half2 accumulator, and incorrectly relates Nc to WGMMA's N tile.

claims.claim: The pinned SM100 DeepGEMM path uses block-scaled tcgen05/UMMA with packed UE8M0 scale factors moved into TMEM and does not use the SM90 CUDA-core final_accum promotion loop.

evidence.locator: make_instr_desc_block_scaled, UTCCP scale-factor copies, MMA issue loop, and TMEM epilogue
evidence.observation: The instruction descriptor selects float_ue8m0_t scaling, scale-factor data is copied from shared memory to TMEM, and UMMA accumulates to TMEM without the SM90 final_accum loop.

challenge.alternative: SM100 simply reuses the SM90 WGMMA-plus-FP32-register promotion path.
challenge.check: Trace the scale factors and accumulator destination in both pinned files.
challenge.outcome: The SM100 file constructs a block-scaled UMMA descriptor and names TMEM columns for scales and accumulators; it has no SM90-style final_accum promotion loop.

claims.claim: The displayed SM100 inline PTX correctly packs scale values in a general register, passes them directly to a short tcgen05.mma form, and establishes full-precision TMEM accumulation.

evidence.locator: instruction descriptor, UTCCP copies, SM100_MMA_MXF8F6F4_SS::fma, and epilogue
evidence.observation: The pinned implementation places packed scale-factor data in TMEM, supplies TMEM scale addresses and a runtime instruction descriptor through a CUTLASS UMMA wrapper, and does not make the page's blanket full-precision claim. The displayed hand-written assembly is not the implementation.

claims.claim: All three illustrated grouped-GEMM modes vary only M with fixed N/K, masked mode uses a binary mask, and the displayed prefix-offset/binary-search CUDA function represents DeepGEMM's contiguous scheduler.

evidence.observation: M-grouped contiguous/masked interfaces keep N and K fixed, masked_m is an int vector of valid M lengths, and K-grouped interfaces instead keep M/N fixed with per-group K lengths. The real contiguous layout may be per-row group IDs or a prefix-sum layout and does not use the invented function.
The project distinguishes M-axis contiguous/masked APIs from a K-axis-grouped weight-backward API.

claims.claim: DeepGEMM uses NVRTC JIT by default and the displayed jit_compile API faithfully shows per-shape compilation that guarantees optimal register allocation and unrolling.

evidence.observation: The JIT defaults to NVCC; NVRTC is selected only when DG_JIT_USE_NVRTC=1. Generated code is cached by a signature over name/compiler/flags/code. The page's jit_compile call is not a repository API and neither source guarantees an optimal result.
The README explicitly describes the low-overhead JIT C++ module and documents NVRTC as optional, disabled by default, and potentially lower-performing for some cases.

claims.claim: The pinned library supports only NT for SM90 FP8 operands and exposes NT, TN, NN, and TT dense layouts for SM100, implemented through SM100 operand-major choices and API wrappers.

evidence.observation: The README explicitly scopes SM90 to NT and SM100 to all four layouts.
The API wrappers and SM100 major parameters realize the documented interface while the SM90 checks require K-major operands.

challenge.alternative: All four public names merely alias an NT kernel with no layout-specific operand handling on SM100.
challenge.check: Trace the nn/tn/tt wrappers and major selection into the SM100 implementation.
challenge.outcome: The wrappers transpose the relevant tensor views and the SM100 template receives corresponding operand-major values; SM90 rejects the non-K-major cases.

claims.claim: DeepGEMM measured 1550 TFLOPS and about 90% utilization on H800 specifically for M=N=K=4096.

evidence.observation: The source reports only up to 1550 TFLOPS on H800; it does not attach M=N=K=4096 or a 90% utilization calculation.
The disclosed peak before later changes is associated with M=4096, N=7168, K=16384, while the listed shapes and values do not include a 1550-TFLOPS 4096-cubed result.

claims.claim: The documented fine-grained scaled GEMMs are applicable to FP8 training/inference and M-grouped MoE computation with variable per-expert token counts.

evidence.observation: The report describes the scheme in training and its deployment/inference context.

evidence.locator: Grouped GEMMs, contiguous and masked layouts
evidence.observation: The project explicitly targets varying token counts per expert for prefill/training and masked decoding.

challenge.alternative: The fine-grained format is only a paper training recipe and DeepGEMM cannot schedule variable expert token counts.
challenge.check: Inspect the pinned grouped API documentation and implementation inputs.
challenge.outcome: The pinned library exports contiguous and masked M-grouped paths whose layout/length tensors encode per-expert work.

claims.claim: A JIT cache miss adds compilation/loading work to the first invocation for a generated kernel signature, while later matching calls may reuse the cached CUBIN/runtime.

evidence.locator: Compiler::build cache lookup, compile, atomic rename, and runtime load
evidence.observation: A signature-keyed cache is checked first; misses compile a CUBIN and create the cache entry, and hits return the existing runtime.

challenge.alternative: Every call recompiles, or installation precompiles every GEMM specialization.
challenge.check: Follow Compiler::build on cache hit and miss and compare with the README installation statement.
challenge.outcome: The hit path returns before compilation and the README says no CUDA compilation is required during installation.

claims.claim: Fine-grained scaling necessarily adds overhead relative to per-tensor scaling and is beneficial only when outlier sensitivity matters.

evidence.observation: The authors describe scale multiplication as having minimal additional computational cost when combined with CUDA-core promotion, but provide no universal per-tensor performance comparison or 'only beneficial' rule. Precision, representable range, native block-scaling support, and integration costs are separate considerations.

claims.claim: The two source links identify the DeepGEMM upstream repository and the DeepSeek-V3 technical report.

evidence.observation: The link resolves to the official DeepGEMM repository.
The link resolves to the DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report.

challenge.alternative: One link is a secondary repost or refers to a different project/paper.
challenge.check: Compare repository owner/title and arXiv title/authors with the page labels.
challenge.outcome: Both resolve to the named first-party project artifacts.

evidence.command: sha256sum artifacts/kernels/deepgemm/full/sm90_fp8_gemm_1d1d.cuh artifacts/kernels/deepgemm/full/sm100_fp8_gemm_1d1d.cuh; conda run -n base python scripts/get_page.py kernel-deepgemm --include-code
evidence.result: Both hashes match the provenance manifest and get_page exits successfully with the page and bundled code.
evidence.negative_control: Changing the page id to kernel-not-deepgemm is rejected rather than returning this page.

challenge.check: Compare manifest modes and hashes, then execute the documented lookup through the repository tool.
challenge.outcome: The full assets are marked verbatim and hash-match; variants are marked derived; the query returned 2477 lines including the linked code.
